title: Extension of scalars to $E$ is a localization on bounded constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\cO_E$, and let $X$ be a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian. Then the functor
$E\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\cO_E}-\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)\to
D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$ of [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-extend-scalars]
is a localization functor with respect to the class $W_{\ell^{\mathbf N}}$
[sk-def-sfb-rationalization]. This is the class of morphisms of the triangulated
$\mathbf Z$-linear category $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$
[sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] whose mapping cone is killed by some power $\ell^n$.

proof.text: Put $A_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $B_T=E_T$ for every scheme $T$, and $A=A_X$, $B=B_X$. The item's map $\varphi\colon A_X\to B_X$ is $p_X^*$ of the condensed inclusion [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield], with $p_X^*=\pi_X^*\circ\mathrm{sheafify}\circ\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{\mathrm{op}}}$ and $u(S)=\operatorname{Spec}LC(S,\mathbf Z)$ [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. Give $E$ the absolute value restricted from $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a norm extending that of $\mathbf Q_\ell$; then the same formula $p_T^*=\pi_T^{-1}\circ a^*$, $a(S)=\operatorname{Spec}LC(S,\mathbf Z)$, applied to the same topological rings $C(-,\mathcal O_E)\to C(-,E)$ defines the pulled-back condensed topological rings, with the actual inclusion $A_T\to B_T$, of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients] and [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. So these coincide by definition. Internal modules and sectionwise ring-sheaf modules are identified by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]: the underlying abelian sheaves and their sections are unchanged. In particular free modules, finite presentations, exact sequences and their derived categories correspond. Let $\mathcal T,\mathcal T'$ be the two full bounded constructible categories in the statement. Their constructibility is the stratified local-finite-presentation predicate in the CURRENT statement of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], equivalently [def-sfb-constructible-module]. It is exactly the predicate used by the integral- and rational-coefficient tools just cited. No equality with finite constant local models is assumed.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.1, 6.8.8, 6.8.10; coefficient/predicate identifications through the cited generic ring-object interfaces

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-serre] the integral constructible modules are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions; [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-constructible-serre] says the same for the finite rational field $E$. Both apply to schemes with Noetherian underlying space, with precisely the coefficients and local-finite-presentation predicate fixed in step 1. Zero and isomorphism invariance follow directly from that predicate. The conditional triangulated-subcategory assertion of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] now applies to both categories. Thus $\mathcal T,\mathcal T'$ inherit their shifts and distinguished triangles. Their additive Hom groups give the canonical $\mathbf Z$-linear structure, and additive shifts preserve integer multiplication.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.9 and Proposition 6.8.11; the two cited Serre lemmas supply the generic-predicate comparison inputs

proof.text: By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], $B=A[1/\ell]=\varinjlim(A\xrightarrow{\ell}A\to\cdots)$ and $B$ is flat. For a K-flat resolution $P\to K$, the computation in [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] gives $F(K)=B\otimes_AP$. Exact tensor takes $P\to K$ to a quasi-isomorphism, so this identifies $F$ canonically with termwise ordinary tensor on derived categories. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] this functor is triangulated. Its restriction to $\mathcal T\to\mathcal T'$ is defined by [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-bounded-constructible] and is exactly [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-extend-scalars]. For all termwise tensor and colimit calculations below use the small skeleton of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in its larger universe. We use ordinary module sheaves, without completion.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); blueprint opening paragraph

proof.text: The functor $F$ is additive, so if $\ell^n\operatorname{id}_Z=0$ then $\ell^n\operatorname{id}_{FZ}=0$. Multiplication by $\ell$ on $FZ$ is invertible because it is so on $B$ [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell]; composing with its inverse gives $\operatorname{id}_{FZ}=0$, so $FZ$ is zero. For a morphism in $W_{\ell^{\mathbf N}}$, apply $F$ to its cone triangle. Its cone is now zero, so [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] makes the image arrow an isomorphism. The localization universal property in [sk-def-sfb-rationalization] therefore gives a factor $\bar F:\mathcal T[\ell^{-1}]\to\mathcal T'$.

Use the Verdier localization model whose objects are those of $\mathcal T$. Let $Q:\mathcal T\to\mathcal T[\ell^{-1}]$ be the rationalization. Apply [lem-sfb-rationalization-scalar-fractions] with $R=\mathbf Z$ and $M=\{\ell^n:n\ge0\}$. The canonical map
$$\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,L)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T[\ell^{-1}]}(QK,QL),\qquad [f,n]\longmapsto\ell^{-n}Q(f),$$
where transitions multiply by $\ell$, is surjective by clause 1. If $\ell^{-n}Q(f)=\ell^{-m}Q(g)$, multiply by $\ell^{n+m}$ and use clause 2 to obtain an $r\ge0$ with $\ell^{r+m}f=\ell^{r+n}g$. These are exactly the representatives of the two classes at stage $n+m+r$, proving injectivity. Invertibility of the scalar maps is part of [sk-def-sfb-rationalization]. This proves the localized Hom formula, with its specified canonical map.

Fix a sequence $D_n$ of complexes of $A$-modules with a common cohomological lower bound and a termwise colimit cocone $c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-sheaf-hom], every constructible integral sheaf $M$ satisfies $H(D,c)(M[0])$ as defined in [def-weil-pbc-hom-colimit-property]. The sheaf hypothesis here is the stratified local-finite-presentation predicate of step 1. The condition is invariant under shifts, since replacing $M[0]$ by $M[0][r]$ replaces the target shift $q$ by $q-r$. It holds for zero since both Hom groups vanish.

For bounded constructible $K$ with cohomology in $[a,b]$, [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] gives successive triangles
$$\tau_{\le r-1}K\longrightarrow\tau_{\le r}K\longrightarrow H^r(K)[-r]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\le r-1}K)[1].$$
Indeed the quotient of these smart truncations is the complex $\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}\hookrightarrow\ker d^r$ in degrees $r-1,r$, and projection onto $H^r(K)[-r]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Each $H^r(K)$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Start with $\tau_{\le a-1}K=0$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-colimit-extension] for $r=a,\ldots,b$. Since $\tau_{\le b}K\simeq K$, the canonical maps
$$\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(K,QD_n[q])\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(K,Qc_\infty[q])$$
are isomorphisms for every $q$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and bounded truncation induction; the cited sheaf-source theorem supplies continuity for the current predicate

proof.text:
For $L\in\mathcal T$ choose a bounded-below complex $L^\bullet$ representing it, using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. The sequence with every term $L^\bullet$ and transition $\ell$ has termwise colimit representing $\operatorname{Res}_A^BF(L)$. In fact [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell] and tensor-colimit compatibility [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor] identify it with $B\otimes_AL^\bullet$, and step 3 identifies ordinary with derived tensor. The terms have a common lower bound; exactness of filtered colimits also preserves that bound. Apply step 6 and the extension/restriction adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] to obtain
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T'}(FK,FL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(K,\operatorname{Res}FL)\cong\varinjlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,L).$$
The ambient $D(A)$ is necessary since $\operatorname{Res}FL$ need not be integral constructible. The $n$-th colimit leg is $\ell^{-n}$ times the adjunction unit: this follows from the coefficient colimit legs $\ell^{-n}\varphi$. Consequently the displayed comparison sends $[f,n]$ to $\ell^{-n}F(f)$. Comparing with the same canonical map in step 5 proves that the factor $\bar F$ is fully faithful. We use the same-object Verdier localization model of step 5, so this covers every quotient object.

The essential image of the original functor $F$ is closed under cones. Given an arrow $a:FK\to FL$, the canonical Hom comparison in steps 5–7 writes $a=\ell^{-n}F(f)$ for some $f:K\to L$ and $n\ge0$. Complete $f$ to a distinguished triangle in $\mathcal T$ by TR1 [def-weil-triangulated-category] and apply the triangulated functor $F$ of step 3. Its first arrow is $F(f)$. Complete $a$ to a distinguished triangle in $\mathcal T'$. The vertical maps $\ell^n\operatorname{id}_{FK}$ on the first vertex and $\operatorname{id}_{FL}$ on the second give a commuting first square, since $a\circ\ell^n=F(f)$, and both are isomorphisms. TR3 extends them to a morphism of triangles; [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes its third component an isomorphism. Thus the given cone is isomorphic to $F$ of the integral cone. Endpoint isomorphisms handle objects merely isomorphic to $FK,FL$. Rotation gives extension closure, and exactness of $F$ gives zero and shift closure. Consequently all objects constructed by these operations from integral images belong to the image of $F$, hence also to the image of $\bar F$. This uses fractions and invertible scalars, not fullness of the original integral functor.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), finite-cone closure of the fully faithful factor

proof.text: Let $M$ be a constructible $B$-module. The current definition [def-sfb-constructible-module] supplies a finite stratification on each stratum of which $M$ is locally finitely presented. Every stratum has Noetherian underlying space. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality] to each restriction: it is lisse, namely locally finite free over the SAME pulled-back condensed $E$-ring, not a constant discrete ring. Apply [lem-sfb-topological-stratified-lisse-lattices] on these strata. On a further finite stratification, each restriction has an integral lisse lattice $L_{0,S}$ with $B_S\otimes_{A_S}L_{0,S}\cong M|_S$. Local freeness implies local finite presentation by the presentation with zero relation module. Thus these are integral constructible sheaves in the required generic sense. No global lisse lattice is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13 first paragraph; the cited local-triviality bridge supplies the extra generic-predicate input

proof.text: For an open–closed cut $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ of a topologically Noetherian scheme, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] gives exact $j_!,i_*$ and the four restriction identities. The coefficient identifications are the untwisted ones of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], requiring no invertibility of $\ell$ on $T$. These extension functors preserve the constructibility of [def-sfb-constructible-module]: take the finite presentation stratification in their domain, view its strata in $T$, and append the complementary subset with the zero module. The restriction identities give the original presentations on the domain strata and the zero presentation on the complement. A stratum closed in an open of the domain is still locally closed in $T$; composition of its immersion with the domain immersion is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Every open subset of a Noetherian space is quasi-compact, so all complements here are quasi-compact and all the schemes here are qcqs (intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact). These are the hypotheses of the ringed theorem.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), extension of integral generators by open–closed cuts

proof.text:
The extensions of step 10 commute with localization. Express $B_T\otimes_{A_T}N$ as $\varinjlim(N\xrightarrow{\ell}N\to\cdots)$, using [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell] and [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. The closed functor $i_*$ preserves this colimit by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. For $j_!$, the stated adjunction gives, for any $P$, $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!\varinjlim N_n,P)=\operatorname{Hom}(\varinjlim N_n,j^{-1}P)=\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N_n,P)$, so its colimit comparison is an isomorphism. All functors are coefficient-linear, hence send each transition $\ell$ to $\ell$. With the coefficient identifications of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], the colimit legs therefore give
$$B_T\otimes_{A_T}e(N)\cong e(B_{\mathrm{domain}}\otimes_{A_{\mathrm{domain}}}N),\qquad e=j_!\text{ or }i_*.$$
Finite composites of these extensions are exact, preserve constructibility by step 10, and commute with localization by composing the displayed isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), localization of integral generators; explicit colimit comparison

proof.text: Refine the finite partition from step 9 by a finite tree of open–closed cuts. Its stratum immersions into $X$ are composites of immersions, hence immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). For each such $S\hookrightarrow X$ choose a factorization $S\hookrightarrow U\hookrightarrow X$ as closed then open [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. On a current branch $T\to X$, first cut by the inverse-image open $T_U=T\times_XU$ and its closed complement; inside $T_U$ cut by $T_S=T\times_XS$ and its open complement. The pulled-back closed immersion is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b); on affine charts it is defined by the extended ideal. Thus the branch $T_S$ has an ACTUAL morphism to $S$. Process the finitely many strata on all branches. A nonempty final leaf cannot be in the complement of every stratum, since their images cover $X$; it therefore maps to a stratum $S$. Every leaf is topologically Noetherian. Pull $L_{0,S}$ back to this leaf $V$: finite free trivializations and their inverse transition matrices pull back, and the coefficient isomorphism of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies its rationalization with $M|_V$. This gives integral lisse $L_{0,V}$. Empty branches are omitted. This finite procedure uses scheme-theoretic pullbacks throughout; set containment alone is never used to factor a scheme morphism.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), finite refinement of the lattice strata by open–closed cuts

proof.text:
For a vertex $T$ of this finite tree, record its path extension $P_T$ to $X$, with $P_X=\operatorname{id}$. At a cut with open child $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ and closed child $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$, set $P_U=P_Tj_!$ and $P_Z=P_Ti_*$. Steps 10–11 show that these are exact, preserve constructibility and commute with localization. At a leaf $V$ the integral constructible sheaf $P_VL_{0,V}$ consequently satisfies
$$F((P_VL_{0,V})[0])\cong(P_V(M|_V))[0].$$
Here ordinary tensor computes $F$ by step 3. Thus the leaf object is in the essential image. This argument records the exact path functor used; it does not require a factorization-independent extension functor for arbitrary locally closed immersions.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), leaf generators and path extensions

proof.text:
At a vertex $T$ the short exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] is
$$0\to j_!(M|_U)\to M|_T\to i_*(M|_Z)\to0.$$
Apply the exact path functor $P_T$ and use [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]. The resulting distinguished triangle has vertices $(P_U(M|_U))[0]$, $(P_T(M|_T))[0]$, $(P_Z(M|_Z))[0]$. By step 13 the leaf vertices are in the image. Backwards induction on the finite tree, using extension closure from step 8, puts every parent vertex in the image. At the root this proves $M[0]$ is in the image. If $X$ is empty, only the zero object occurs.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), reconstruction from integral generators

proof.text: For $K'\in\mathcal T'$ with cohomology in $[a,b]$, use [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] and the successive-truncation calculation in step 6. Begin with $\tau_{\le a-1}K'=0$. Each $H^r(K')$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], so step 14 and shift closure from step 8 put $H^r(K')[-r]$ in the image. Successive extension closure for $r=a,\ldots,b$ puts $\tau_{\le b}K'\simeq K'$ in the image. This proves essential surjectivity. The argument also covers a single nonzero cohomology degree and the zero complex.

A fully faithful essentially surjective functor is an equivalence: choose for each target object an isomorphism from an image object, and use the bijections on Hom groups to define the inverse on morphisms; uniqueness makes identities and composition commute. Hence $\bar F$ is an equivalence. Since $F=\bar FQ$ and $Q$ is localization at the specified torsion-cone class [sk-def-sfb-rationalization], $F$ has the same localization universal property. This is the assertion.
